chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Accurate T-staging is crucial for guiding personalized treatment strategies for laryngopharyngeal cancer. However, current clinical practice relies on invasive biopsy procedures, whereas CT-based staging remains challenging due to the complex patterns of tumor invasion.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem, including the challenges of CT-based staging and the limitations of existing methods, matching the reference.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: We propose an anatomy-aware multimodal framework that integrates organ-level CT context and radiology reports into a unified representation for laryngopharyngeal T-staging. The framework first constructs an Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG) that captures invasion patterns between primary sites and surrounding organs, then performs Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA) so that each organ node aggregates textual evidence from the radiology report, and finally refines this graph representation by injecting organ-specific invasion cues extracted from the report via Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG).
chk_method.reason: The poster provides a detailed description of the method, including its components (AOG, OCA, REG), aligning with the reference.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: We collect the first and largest dataset for CT-based laryngopharyngeal cancer T-staging, comprising 656 patients across four medical centers, all paired with CT reports for multimodal assessment.
chk_data.reason: The poster specifies the dataset size, composition, and paired CT scans and radiology reports, matching the reference.

chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: We introduced an anatomy-structured multimodal framework for laryngopharyngeal cancer T-staging that integrates CT volumes and paired radiology reports.
